memory_candidates.content: check-module-invariants.sh's generated inventory blocks (per-file line-count tables in README.md/*.md, delimited by <!-- BEGIN GENERATED: inventory --> fences) go stale whenever a docstring-only edit changes a Lean file's line count, even though nothing structural changed. A docstring/documentation-only task should not assume it is exempt from this gate; run `bash scripts/check-module-invariants.sh --emit-inventory` to mechanically regenerate the stale blocks (a pure line-count/comment-count rewrite, not a hand-authored change) before declaring the invariants gate green.

check-module-invariants.sh's C1 check runs a full `lake build` plus `lake build BimodalTest` in the foreground, which on a large Lean project can run long enough to be killed by a host-level low-memory reaper when launched as a background Bash task. Most other checks (including C15, the paper-anchor gate) do not depend on the build and can be verified quickly via `--no-build`. When the full run is interrupted, corroborate C1 with independent evidence instead of blindly re-running the full script: check .lake/build-guard.log for a recent green full build, or run a guarded scoped build over the specific touched modules/aggregators via lake-build-guard.sh.
